# @visio/scroll: design

Smooth scrolling for a visio site. Every darkroom site ran Lenis on the tempus loop. This package is that setup for Solid 2: `<SmoothScroll />` mounts Lenis on the window, steps it in the first slot of the frame loop of `@visio/frame`, and keeps it out of the router's way. The loop itself is `@visio/frame` (`packages/frame/DESIGN.md`).

Lenis is optional. A site that keeps the native scroll leaves `<SmoothScroll />` out, and its code does not change: it scrolls and locks the page with `scrollTo()` and `lockScroll()`, which use Lenis when it runs and the browser when it does not. Only a WebGL object on a canvas fixed over the viewport, which follows a page element, needs Lenis: on the native scroll it trails by a frame (the `frame` skill, `references/webgl.md`).

## Requirements

1. Smooth scrolling that never fights the router. A link resets scroll to the top, back and forward restore a saved offset, and both have to stick even when a wheel flick is still gliding.
2. Lenis moves the page before anything else in the frame, so whatever reads the scroll sees this frame's value.
3. Nothing on the server, and nothing that shifts hydration.
4. The Lenis instance is app-wide state, reachable from any component without a provider.
5. A site toggles Lenis by adding or removing `<SmoothScroll />`, and no other line changes.

## The design

### API

- `<SmoothScroll />`: place it once, inside the router. It creates Lenis on mount with `autoRaf: false`, since the loop drives it. It reads the props once, at mount. It destroys Lenis on unmount. A second one warns in dev: the server render prints the warning in the dev server's terminal (one flag per request, from `getRequestEvent()`), and the browser warns for one that only the client mounts. Its props are the feel of the glide: `lerp`, `duration` and `easing`, which Lenis 2 takes for the wheel (`wheel`) and for `scrollTo` (`programmatic`), and `wheelMultiplier` (`wheel.multiplier`). They keep the names of Lenis 1, where one option set both. An unset prop is left out, not passed as `undefined`: Lenis spreads each group over its defaults, and an `undefined` would replace one ([#553](https://github.com/darkroomengineering/lenis/issues/553); remove `defined()` when it is fixed). Everything else is fixed: reduced motion is on, and `anchors` and `stopInertiaOnNavigate` are off, because the package glides to same-page anchors itself (see Anchors below).
- `lenis()`: the instance, a module-scope signal. Undefined on the server, without `<SmoothScroll />`, and before mount. Use it for reading `scroll`, `velocity` or `progress` inside a frame callback. It lives in `src/instance.ts`, so a site that imports only the helpers does not bundle Lenis.
- `scrollTo(target, { offset, immediate })`: Lenis's `scrollTo` when it runs. Without it, `window.scrollTo` with `behavior: 'smooth'`, or `'instant'` under reduced motion or with `immediate`. The target is a pixel offset, a selector or an `HTMLElement`, the types of `lenis().scrollTo`. Without Lenis it lands where Lenis 2 would (`resolveScrollTargets()`): the keywords `top`, `start`, `#`, `bottom` and `end`, `#id` by `getElementById`, and an element's top less its `scroll-margin-top` and the root's `scroll-padding-top`. An element lands where Lenis would land it: its top, less its `scroll-margin-top`, plus `offset`. The options are the two that both ways can honour; Lenis's `duration`, `easing`, `lock` and the rest have no native match. An SVG element is a type error: Lenis reads its own `x` and `y` as a position ([#551](https://github.com/darkroomengineering/lenis/issues/551)). A selector that matches nothing leaves the page and warns in dev.
- `lockScroll()`: `overflow: hidden` on `<html>`, which stops the wheel, touch, the keyboard and the scrollbar, and `lock()` on Lenis when it runs. Where a scrollbar takes width, the lock also sets `scrollbar-gutter: stable`, so the page does not shift. It returns the release of this one lock. The page scrolls again when every lock is released, and the last release puts back the inline `overflow` and `scrollbar-gutter` that were there before. A second call of a release does nothing. A shared `unlockScroll()` was in the first draft: a modal that unlocked on close and again in `onCleanup` released the lock of a menu that was still open.
- The package does not export the `Lenis` class or `LenisOptions`, and lint bans an import of `lenis` in the site and the lab. A second instance, or one with other options, would fight the router.

### How the parts fit

- **The loop.** Lenis runs on the loop of `@visio/frame` with `order: ORDER.scroll`, labelled `lenis`, so a callback at `ORDER.animation` reads this frame's scroll (`drive` in `src/smooth-scroll.ts`). It keeps the loop running while it glides (`isScrolling` is `'smooth'`), and lets it sleep otherwise. It wakes the loop on a gesture (its `gesture` event), on each `scroll` event, which a native scroll emits too, so a callback that reads the scroll runs once for it, and on `scrollTo`. Lenis has no event for `scrollTo`, so `drive` wraps the instance's method and puts it back on unmount. A native scroll needs no frame from Lenis: the browser moves the page, and Lenis only records it.
- **The router.** Solid Router scrolls the window itself: `scrollTo(0, 0)` after a link, and the saved offset once a back or forward navigation settles. That restore comes before `@visio/transitions` has mounted the returning page, so the outlet restores the offset again once the page has settled (`packages/transitions/DESIGN.md`). Lenis only follows an outside scroll while it is idle; mid-glide, it would carry on toward its own target and drag the page away from where the router put it. So `SmoothScroll` stops the glide twice: when a navigation starts (`useBeforeLeave`), and when it commits (an effect on the location and `isRouting`). The second one matters when the page loads slowly: a wheel during the load starts a new glide, and the router only scrolls at the commit. It stops the glide with Lenis's `reset()`, which is private in Lenis's types but public at runtime. `scrollTo(y, { immediate: true })` is not the same: it also ignores the next native scroll event, and that event can be the router's.
- **Anchors.** A plain left click on a link to a hash on the same page (same origin, path and query) glides to the target. `SmoothScroll` listens for clicks on the document in the capture phase, before the router's handler, and calls `scrollTo(target)` on Lenis. It does not call `preventDefault()`, so the router still takes the click: it pushes the URL with the hash, and back and forward work as for any link. The router also jumps to the target, but Lenis is mid-glide and ignores that scroll. The navigation stops the glide twice (see the router above); for this one click, `stopGlide` does nothing until the next task. The glide ends where the router's jump would: Lenis subtracts the target's `scroll-margin-top`, as `scrollIntoView()` does.
- **Anchors without Lenis.** The router jumps to the target (`scrollIntoView()`). CSS `scroll-behavior: smooth` cannot make it glide: the router's reset after a link is `window.scrollTo(0, 0)` with no `behavior`, so the CSS would make every page change glide to the top too, and the outlet's restore with it. The styling compiler rejects it for that reason. A glide for anchors without Lenis would need a component in app.tsx; it is not built until a site asks.
- **When anchors jump.** The router jumps, and nothing glides, in these cases: a hash link to another page (the target is not on the page yet), a click with a modifier key or another button, a link with `target`, `download` or `noscroll`, a hash with no element, while Lenis is locked, and under reduced motion. Lenis's own `anchors` option cannot work under the router (see the facts below), so it is not in the props.
- **CSS.** The package declares Lenis's stylesheet in `visio.stylesheets` of its `package.json`, and the styling sheet takes it in its `reset` layer (`styling/DESIGN.md`, "Package stylesheets"). The page must not set `scroll-behavior: smooth` on `html`: the router's reset has to land in one step, and Lenis does the gliding.
- **Reduced motion.** Lenis's own `respectReducedMotion` is always on: the scroll tracks the input 1:1, programmatic scrolls jump, and anchors jump. Without Lenis, `scrollTo` reads `reducedMotion()` from `@visio/frame` and jumps.
- **Nested scrollers.** With Lenis, mark them `data-lenis-prevent` (or `-wheel`, `-touch`) so the wheel scrolls them and not the page. Without Lenis the attribute does nothing, and the browser scrolls them.

### Rules for components

- Call `onSettled` on the server as well, even when it only does client work. A Solid 2 component has no owner of its own, so an `onSettled` inside it takes a hydration id from the parent. One registered on the client only shifts every id after it, and whatever comes next in the tree fails to hydrate: the nav, the page and the footer when `SmoothScroll` sits first in the app. `SmoothScroll` follows this, as `useFrame` does. `useBeforeLeave` registers a listener, not a computation, so it can stay client-only, as it does in `@visio/transitions`. A client-only effect is created with `{ transparent: true }`, which takes no hydration id; the router does the same for its scroll restore.

## Facts checked against the installed versions

Lenis 2.0.0-dev.5, without dependencies.

- Lenis's `onNativeScroll` syncs to the window only while `isScrolling` is `false` or `'native'`. `reset()` sets `isScrolling` to `false`, syncs the target to the window and stops the animation. `scrollTo(x, { immediate: true })` does that too, and then ignores the next native scroll event until Lenis's next animation frame. A browser dispatches scroll events before animation frame callbacks, so the router's `scrollTo(0, 0)` in the same frame is lost.
- Lenis sets `isScrolling` to `'native'` on each scroll event and back to `false` 400 ms after the last one, also when the page did not move. In Lenis 1 the timer started only when the page moved, so after `reset()` the router's scroll left `lenis-scrolling` on `<html>` ([#550](https://github.com/darkroomengineering/lenis/issues/550)), and the package had a workaround until Lenis 2.
- `reset()` is not in the types of Lenis 2 either, but it is a method at runtime. Remove the cast in `stopGlide` when Lenis makes it public ([#554](https://github.com/darkroomengineering/lenis/issues/554)).
- Lenis 2 turns `anchors` and `stopInertiaOnNavigate` on by default; the package turns both off. A page whose overflow is `hidden` or `clip` does not scroll with Lenis 2: `lenis.css` puts a transition on `overflow`, and Lenis reads the overflow again when it ends. Lenis 1 needed `autoToggle` for that.
- `anchors` matches links with the same host and path and a hash, from a click listener on the window. The router's click handler listens on the document, so it runs first. After each listener of a trusted click, the browser runs the microtasks, so the router's navigation (its stop, its jump) completes before Lenis's window listener runs. Lenis then measures the target from a scroll position it has not synced. It does nothing, or it glides the page back. A click from a script (`el.click()`) runs all the listeners in one go, and the microtasks after them, so a test with `el.click()` shows the opposite order. `SmoothScroll` listens on the document in the capture phase, which comes before both, for trusted clicks and for script clicks.
- `stopInertiaOnNavigate` only covers link clicks to another path, not history traversals, so the router hook is used instead, and the option is off.
- The router scrolls in `history.set`, from an `onSettled` after the navigation's write, so at the commit and not at the click. Back and forward restore from an `onSettled` after the traversal's write. A reload or a document load from history is the browser's own restore: the router sets `scrollRestoration` to `auto` on `pagehide` and back to `manual` after `load` (since 2.0.0-next.37).

## Scroll progress

`useScrollProgress(element, { start, end })` (`progress.ts`) reads the element's box in a frame callback at `ORDER.animation`, after Lenis moves the page in the same frame, so a value read by an animation or a draw in that frame is never a frame behind. The callback returns `false`: Lenis keeps the loop running while it glides, and a `scroll` event (in the capture phase, so a nested scroller's counts too), a `resize`, or a change of the page's height (a `ResizeObserver` on `<html>`, for an accordion that opens above the box or a `<Loading>` that resolves) wakes it, so the loop still sleeps while the page is still. `progressOf()` is the arithmetic, tested on its own: each edge is the scroll at which a line of the element meets a line of the viewport, and the value is how far the scroll is from the first to the second, clamped to 0 to 1. The lab case `/scroll/progress` checks it against the box on the native scroll, frame by frame with Lenis, and after a resize.
